record.result: merged https://github.com/hkjang/clustara/pull/14, released v0.9.275, asset manifest failed
record.title: fix(terminal): a root wipe spelled `r"m" -rf /` passed every gate and ran

notes: Tests verified to be real: I checked out main's versions of commandrisk.go/terminalmode.go/admin_k8s_terminal.go/exec.go while keeping the new tests, and every new test file failed (analyzer: 3 tests, 16 cases; kube: 2 tests, 5 cases; proxy: TestTerminalDenyResolvesQuotedProgramSpellings, 7 cases). Restored afterwards; worktree clean. go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... all pass at HEAD.

The reported gap is real and reachable end to end: internal/proxy/admin_k8s_exec.go:309 gates on classifyTerminalCommandRisk(sess.Command) and internal/proxy/admin_k8s_exec.go:347 then passes the same string as PodExecOptions.Command, which splitCommandLine resolves to argv [rm -rf /]. Pod exec has no shell, so the executor's dequoting was the only parser that saw the real program name.

Direction of change is tightening, not loosening: analyzer/commandrisk.go:215+272 only normalizes more spellings into the same program name, and internal/proxy/admin_k8s_terminal.go:327 adds the normalized form as an extra OR on the deny side only. terminalAllowlistMatches is untouched and TestTerminalAllowlistStaysStrictForQuotedSpellings pins that.

internal/analyzer/shellwords.go:26 and internal/kube/exec.go:626 are two independent copies of the same POSIX word-splitter in different packages. They agree today (I diffed the branches by hand), but the whole point of the fix is that the gate and the executor must not drift; analyzer does not import kube, so kube could call analyzer.ShellWords instead. Worth a follow-up to collapse the duplicate.

internal/kube/exec.go:225 - now that empty words survive splitCommandLine, a Command of `""` yields argv [""] and passes the len(args)==0 check, reaching the exec API with a blank program name; on main it returned "command is required". The CommandArg branch (exec.go:219) does guard this with TrimSpace(out[0])=="", so the two paths are inconsistent. Not a security issue (the gates run upstream and the kubelet rejects an empty argv[0]), just an unreachable-error inconsistency.

internal/analyzer/terminalmode.go:57 - isInteractiveShell now word-splits instead of reading raw bytes, so `bash "-c" ls` is no longer misread as an interactive shell and drops from full_tty (always approval) to the risk-based tier. That is the correct classification (it is not an interactive session) but it is a relaxation relative to main for that one spelling; the payload after -c is still risk-parsed, so `bash "-c" "rm -rf /"` remains critical.

internal/kube/exec.go:626 changes live behaviour for existing users: a backslash inside single quotes is now literal, so `grep 'a\.b' f` searches for a\.b instead of a.b. POSIX-correct and matches what the reviewer saw in the approved string, but it is a behaviour change for already-saved terminal commands, not a pure bug fix.

gofmt -l flags internal/analyzer/shellwords.go (gofmt rewrites the bare '' in the doc comment to a typographic quote). Cosmetic only - the repo has no .github/workflows and many pre-existing files under internal/analyzer are already gofmt-unclean, so nothing enforces it.

Pre-existing and not introduced here: parameter-expansion spellings such as `sh -c 'rm${IFS}-rf${IFS}/'` still evade the analyzer tokenizer (only $( and ` are flagged as substitution). The executor cannot run those either without a shell, so the gate/executor pair stays consistent, but a `sh -c` payload using ${IFS} would.
Reversibility: pure in-process classification and argv-building logic. No migration, no schema change, no external state, no dependency change. A plain revert restores main's behaviour exactly.
